concepts.gloss_en: the still and pure air — the calm atmosphere of rest produced by love/tzedakah, in which spirits repose one in another

reason_for_human: Both forms occur in the same Torah 17 passage describing the same idea: the calm/pure air generated by love-through-tzedakah where spirits rest in one another. In paragraph 17_5_2 the shorter 'אֲוִיר הַנָּח' and longer 'אֲוִיר הַנָּח וְהַזַּךְ' appear side by side referring to the identical concept — the short form simply drops 'and pure,' which is phrase-length variation, not a distinct word. No homograph or archetype/generic split is present.
